description: ChronoHeritage benchmark suite v1 (PRD §12.4, Appendix D). Independent of the site dataset: all inputs are generic latitudes/epochs, not registry records.
frozen_by: Proposed by the implementation team from PRD v2.0 §12.4 proposed tolerances; frozen before any candidate output was inspected; awaiting domain-reviewer sign-off.

modern.rationale: PRD §12.4: ≤0.10° when directly comparable (matched target, TT instants, airless apparent topocentric az/el, WGS84 site).

historical.rationale: PRD §12.4: ≤0.25° for supported historical cases; both independent paths must agree with the candidate.

published.rationale: Match the reported method and precision of the published case; explain discrepancies (PRD §12.4).

reproducibility.rationale: Bitwise-identical deterministic output for the same seed, inputs, code and environment.

missing_data.rationale: No fabricated values: the calculation must refuse or degrade explicitly.

cases.title: Sun airless apparent az/el, mid-latitude northern site, June 2024
cases.independence_note: JPL Horizons uses JPL's own DE-series ephemeris and reduction software, independent of the Skyfield code path. Both ultimately rest on JPL ephemerides (candidate DE406, Horizons DE441) — disclosed shared lineage.
cases.licence_note: Horizons outputs: cite NASA/JPL Horizons; store numeric extracts and response hash only.

cases.title: Sun airless apparent az/el, southern hemisphere, December 2025
Sun airless apparent az/el, low-latitude site near March equinox 2026
June solstice sunrise azimuth, 51.18°N, 2500 BCE, flat horizon, upper limb
cases.independence_note: Path A (Astropy/ERFA builtin): independent ephemeris (analytic epv00) but shares IAU 2006/2000A precession–nutation with Skyfield. Path B (Laskar 1986 obliquity + low-precision nutation): independent ephemeris and precession. Both paths share the closed-form azimuth relation, Bennett refraction and limb definition with each other; the candidate shares refraction and limb definition only.
cases.licence_note: Astropy (BSD-3), pyerfa (BSD-3); Laskar polynomial as published in Meeus (1998).

cases.title: Circular residual wraparound and axial (modulo 180°) cases
cases.independence_note: Expected values derived by hand from Δ = ((a − b + 180) mod 360) − 180 (directed) and ((a − b + 90) mod 180) − 90 (axial), with the half-open interval convention [−180, 180) / [−90, 90).
